nodes.description: Direct viral cytopathology and apoptosis of infected hepatocytes produce the extensive hepatic necrosis that is the pathological hallmark of fatal RVF - diffuse, with the centrilobular area more affected than the portal area - releasing transaminases and impairing synthesis of coagulation factors.

nodes.description: Interferon antagonism permits rapid systemic dissemination with high-titre viraemia and preferential infection of the liver, the major target organ, where RVFV replicates chiefly in hepatocytes. The magnitude of viraemia correlates with progression to severe disease.

nodes.description: Direct contact with the blood, tissues and aborted material of viraemic livestock - at slaughter, butchering and birthing - is an independent risk factor for acquiring human RVF and the route that establishes infection in herders, abattoir workers and veterinarians. (The broader epizootic that produces viraemic livestock is itself driven by heavy rainfall and flooding expanding the floodwater-Aedes vector population.)

nodes.description: After inoculation RVFV replicates in cells at the site of infection and in the liver and spleen. Its non-structural protein NSs is the principal virulence factor: it suppresses host general transcription and blocks induction of type I interferon, allowing unchecked early viral replication and the high viraemia that drives severe disease.
